subject: sea slug
title: This Sea Slug's Head Drops Off, Then Grows a Whole New Body

scenes.text: This animal's head walks away from its body. On purpose.
It's a Japanese sea slug. Its head pinches itself off and leaves the body behind.
Within hours, some heads are eating again, with no heart.
A new heart starts forming within a week. In about three weeks, it has a whole new body.
Why? Slugs that did it carried parasites. Dropping the body may dump them too.
The headless body keeps twitching for days. It never grows a head back.

description:
Two Japanese sacoglossan sea slugs, Elysia cf. marginata and Elysia atroviridis, can shed their entire body at the neck, and the head goes on to regrow it.
Some detached heads started feeding within hours; the heart began regenerating within about a week and a full new body formed in about three weeks (Mitoh and Yusa, Current Biology, 2021). The shed body, about 80% of the animal, kept moving for days or months but never regrew a head. Slugs that did it carried parasitic copepods, so it may be a way to get rid of them.
Which would you keep, the head or the body?
first_comment: One slug dropped its body and regrew it twice. What is the most extreme regeneration you know?
